clue.text: Dispute from detective in criminal stretch

indicators.note: something placed in another sits inside it, so the detective goes inside the stretch

blocks.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a tract is a stretch of land
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective argues against the length of a criminal's prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: A stretch is also slang for a prison term, which is what the surface wants; here it is a tract of land, split to take DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict someone is to argue against what they said, so the verb matches dispute.

clue.text: Headgear put on English head

blocks.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone places a hat on an Englishman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means placed above, so the headgear comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape or headland is a promontory jutting into the sea, called a head in place names.

clue.text: Almost hurry purchasing women’s pyjamas?

indicators.note: buying is taking something in hand, so the hurry word takes in the women's abbreviation

blocks.note: nigh means almost or nearly
to tear is to rush along
W is the abbreviation for women's

explanation.surface: Someone nearly rushes in to buy ladies' pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks pyjamas as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas are one kind of clothing worn in bed, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Stood for president, say, reversing diversity

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word for say is read from right to left

blocks.note: a candidate runs, past tense ran, for office
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A presidential candidate does a U-turn on diversity policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of things is a varied assortment, so both words describe variety across a spread.

clue.text: Occasionally admits former PM’s troubles

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of admits is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
Theresa May was a British Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's woes are sometimes owned up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to trouble or upset them, so both are verbs about causing distress.

clue.text: Fancy kit’s some underwear

blocks.note: surface: some smart outfit consists partly of undergarments
setter's reading: decorative, boned foundation garments worn under elaborate dress

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: shaped, laced undergarments that are often elaborate costume pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsets are stiffened garments worn beneath clothing to shape the waist, often decorative.

clue.text: Initially cheer, laugh and possibly applaud

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: An audience cheers, laughs and perhaps gives a round of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' reads as a hedge but only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap is to strike the palms together in approval, which is what applauding means.

clue.text: Left foreign port carrying cargo

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship departed an overseas harbour loaded with freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb of departure; it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or weighed down, as a ship heavy with goods aboard.

clue.text: For each sweetheart figure produces effect

blocks.note: per means for each, as in per head
pet is a term of endearment
a rate is a figure, as in a rate of interest

explanation.surface: A statistic per loved one has a measurable impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect' here is the verb meaning bring about, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a deed is to carry it out or commit it, so both verbs mean cause to happen.

clue.text: Carefree woman coming out live

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman making her formal entry into society
a broadcast that is live is on air

explanation.surface: A woman appears in public, broadcast live and untroubled.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante 'comes out' at her first society ball, a British upper-class tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, nonchalant and charming manner, untroubled and light-hearted.

clue.text: Heathen god suppresses endless fury

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters of fury are dropped
to suppress is to hold something down within, so the god keeps the shortened fury inside

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
rage is fury

explanation.surface: A god holds back a boundless rage against unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: With both ends cut, the word for fury keeps only its middle two letters, which Pan then holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan follows a polytheistic or non-mainstream religion, which is what a heathen was called by Christians.

clue.text: Resignation more certain to involve split

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so the word for split is taken into the middle of more certain

blocks.note: comparative of sure
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: Quitting looks the safer bet when it means a rift.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender is giving up or yielding, the same act of acceptance and submission as resignation.

clue.text: Cheapest places, always ancient, inside theatre

indicators.note: inside places the archaic word for always within the word for theatre

blocks.note: the stage stands for the theatre
e'er is the old poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: An old theatre has always had cheap seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' signals the archaic form of always.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-fare accommodation on a passenger ship, below decks.

clue.text: Cat with lunge lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for power is removed from the lunge word

blocks.note: to pounce is to spring forward
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A cat springs forward but feebly.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is another name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a large wild feline of Central Asia, is also called an ounce.

clue.text: Influence of print media covering party

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the print media word goes round the party word

blocks.note: the press is newspapers and magazines
a posse is a group or band

explanation.surface: Newspapers sway opinion by reporting on a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepossess is to influence someone beforehand, to bias them in favour of something.

clue.text: Turns catching end of ankle joints

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the final letter of ankle is used
catching means trapping something within, so the turns word holds that letter inside

blocks.note: one turns to, or refers to, a source
final letter

explanation.surface: Someone twists a foot, catching the end of the ankle joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joints' looks anatomical, given the ankle, but means cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: Demanding former partner creating a scene

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
actors create scenes on stage

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is making a fuss and being difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Making a scene suggests a tantrum; here it is performing a scene in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means requiring great effort or care, so it is an adjective like demanding.

clue.text: Spread first of soap suds

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so soap contributes only its initial

blocks.note: opening letter
lather is soapy foam

explanation.surface: Someone smears on the first of the soap bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To slather is to apply something thickly and liberally, smearing it over a surface.

clue.text: Discover article about a Conservative suffering

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the a plus Conservative letters

blocks.note: to hear of something is to find it out
the definite article
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reveals a Tory politician's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional pain or grief, a noun for the anguish meant by suffering.

clue.text: Carriage left before time

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A carriage departed ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed; it is the nautical left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is the carrying of boats or goods overland between waterways, an act of transport.

clue.text: Feeling of abasement spending penny

indicators.note: spending money means giving it away, so the penny letter is lost from abasement

blocks.note: a demotion is a lowering in rank
d was the symbol for an old British penny

explanation.surface: Losing money brings a feeling of humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a state of mind such as joy or anger, a sentiment the heart experiences.

clue.text: Caustic second harangue about Democrat

indicators.note: about means around, so the harangue word surrounds the Democrat abbreviation

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a rant is a loud tirade
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A cutting second tirade about an American Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is biting and sarcastic, just as a caustic remark stings.

clue.text: Good deal: reduced money for rubber

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the currency word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a mass of something is a good deal of it
the euro is a currency

explanation.surface: A bargain on cheap money for a rubber purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubber reads as the material but is one who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur gives massages, kneading muscles, so he is literally someone who rubs.

clue.text: Go round in some women’s clothing

blocks.note: first meaning: to pass around the edge of something
second meaning: a garment hanging from the waist

explanation.surface: Someone walks about dressed in ladies' garments.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to avoid or circle; as a noun it is a garment worn from the waist.

clue.text: One grand lavatory for cool house

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
loo is British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: A single impressive toilet for a trendy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool house' sounds like a stylish one but means a cold dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit shelter built from blocks of snow, literally a chilly home.

clue.text: Old, old fish in batter, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters of batter
in puts the fish inside the selected letters of batter

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
first, third and fifth letters
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: An old fish fried in batter looks peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish in batter' paints a fish supper, but the batter only lends alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means out of date or no longer in use, outdated just as old things are.

clue.text: Fibbed about woman finally having wrinkles

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of woman is kept
about means surrounding, so the fibbed word goes around that letter

blocks.note: fibbing is telling lies
final letter

explanation.surface: Someone lied about a woman eventually getting wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: A lined face is marked with creases, so the adjective describes skin furrowed with age.

clue.text: Maybe game hunt for the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word for hunt is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a meet is a gathering of a hunt

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a hunt is called a meet, the gathering of riders and hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is the flesh of wild animals eaten as food, an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Worker in such as train plant

indicators.note: in means positioned inside, so the worker goes within the word for train

blocks.note: e.g. means for example
a line of things forms a train
the worker ant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests an industrial works; it is a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose bush with fragrant leaves, so it is a type of shrub.

clue.text: Opening of hotel in French resort

blocks.note: Nice is a resort on the Riviera

explanation.surface: A hotel launch on the French Riviera.

explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess in a wall or a suitable gap, an opening for something to fit into.

clue.text: Drinking red I entertained, taking part

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: I hosted guests while drinking red wine and joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking part' reads as one phrase; split it, 'taking' takes letters from the words before and 'part' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one component of a mixture or recipe, a constituent part of the whole.
